sourceLabel: Audited results filed with BSE and NSE, 14 May 2026
coverage: Whole-group totals · no business segments reported
definition: Profit for the year after all expenses and tax, including HAL’s share of its joint ventures’ profit of ₹43.62 crore. It is not operating profit or cash flow.
location: Filing PDF page 7 (consolidated results, year ended 31-Mar-26 column; scanned copy, no printed page numbers), checked against the BSE consolidated Ind AS filing of 14 May 2026; notes on PDF pages 11–12
notes: Source figures are in ₹ lakh and were divided by 100. Revenue is revenue from operations and excludes other income of ₹3,699.13 crore, which includes interest on deposits (the cash-flow statement shows interest income of ₹3,087.87 crore). Profit is after tax of ₹3,036.41 crore. Two notes in the results change this year’s profit: ₹163.90 crore of salary credited in earlier years was reversed, which lowered profit, and ₹44.99 crore of an earlier provision for flood-damaged customer-owned parts was reversed because the loss turned out smaller, which raised it; together they lowered profit before tax by ₹118.91 crore. HAL also began paying a higher pension contribution for workmen, adding ₹41.45 crore of cost this year. HAL does not report segments, because a government notification exempts defence-production companies from that accounting rule, so it does not disclose profit for aircraft, helicopters, engines or avionics and none is inferred.
insight: HAL reports one combined business, so these totals cannot show which aircraft, helicopter or engine work earns the profit. Interest on its large deposits is outside revenue but inside profit.
